summary: A photo shows an observation tower at the Moses H. Cone estate beside the Blue Ridge Parkway; a trail guide describes a 40-foot fire tower atop the mountain. The sources do not say whether these are one structure. No build date or staffing found.

facts.status: unconfirmed: the trail guide describes the fire tower in present tense; no dated source states current status

access.note: Hike from Moses Cone Manor off Blue Ridge Parkway milepost 294, per a trail guide

resolved_conflicts.explanation: The photo caption calls the tower in the photo an observation tower, located at the Cone estate; the trail guide describes a 40-foot fire tower atop the mountain. The sources do not establish that these are the same structure, so the story reports both descriptions and does not settle the purpose.

notes_for_editor: Thin record. No build date, staffing, fire or fate source was found; the story leaves those out. Two WebSearch calls and six page reads used. A search snippet credited a Carolina Mountain Club guide (carolinamountainclub.org LTC-Northwestern page, which returned 404 on fetch) with a 1900 wooden observatory and a 1954 steel replacement; unverified, so not used. Unread leads: hikingupward.com/NCSP/FlatTopTower and Blue Ridge Parkway Foundation / National Parks Traveler pages on the Flat Top Manor restoration. Trail length figures conflict across snippets and are not used. Current climbing status of the tower is not stated by any source read; do not add one without a source.
